body.html: No.9 Hostel is a small hostel on Maenamkwae Road in Tha Makham, central Kanchanaburi — the same strip lined with restaurants, bars and riverside stays. Opened in 2023, it's still new, a small building with around 9 rooms focused mainly on dorm beds, in both 4-bed and 6-bed configurations. The draw is sleeping in the tourist heart of town on a budget, in a place that's clean and well kept, rather than luxury or hotel-style amenities.

What guests mention most is the cleanliness. The beds, shared bathrooms and communal areas earn consistent praise for being tidy and clean, and the cleanliness scores on booking platforms run high. The dorm bunks have privacy curtains, lockers for your belongings, and comfy mattresses according to many reviews. There's a shared kitchen for cooking your own meals, a washing machine, and a communal fridge and microwave — a big plus for backpackers staying longer.
"So clean and quiet, the owner was lovely and helped us plan trips, and you can walk to the walking street and restaurants — great value at this price."

The other recurring praise is for the owner and staff. Many reviews mention how friendly and helpful they are, recommending things to do, arranging tours, and looking after guests so it feels more like staying at a friend's place than a hostel. The location is a clear advantage too — a few minutes' walk to the walking street and riverside restaurants, about 12 minutes to Kanchanaburi Railway Station, and within walking or cycling distance of the River Kwai Bridge. It suits travellers arriving by train or exploring town on foot without relying on a car.

The thing to know is that No.9 Hostel is a small, quiet hostel rather than a party hostel. Its social-atmosphere score on some platforms isn't high, because the place is fairly quiet and the common space is limited — anyone hoping to meet fellow travellers and socialise every night may find it a little subdued. There are few beds, so it books up quickly on holidays; reserve ahead. And because these are shared dorms, privacy is inherently limited; a small number of reviews note minor etiquette issues, which is normal for dorm sleeping.

In short, No.9 Hostel is a great fit for solo travellers or couples on a budget who want a clean, quiet bed in a good central Kanchanaburi location, walkable to attractions and the River Kwai Bridge. If you value cleanliness, location and a caring owner over a party scene, it delivers good value for the price. But if you're after a lively hostel with social activities, or a private room with full amenities, consider a riverside guesthouse or a higher-tier hotel in town instead. The 8.8 score comes from a fairly small pool of reviews and reflects the preferences of people looking mainly for "clean, quiet, good location, cheap".

A tip from reading through the reviews: book ahead, especially over long weekends and holidays, because beds are few and fill fast. If you plan to cook or do laundry, ask about the shared kitchen and washing machine at check-in, as that's a feature many guests use. And if you want more privacy than a dorm, ask whether you can book a whole dorm room or which bunk position is more private before you reserve.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — No.9 Hostel Kanchanaburi

faq.q: Where in town is No.9 Hostel, and is it near the River Kwai Bridge?
faq.a: It sits at 9 Maenamkwae Road, Tha Makham, in central Kanchanaburi — the restaurant and riverside-stay strip. It's a few minutes' walk to the walking street and restaurants, about 12 minutes' walk to Kanchanaburi Railway Station, and within walking or cycling distance of the River Kwai Bridge (about 2–3 km).

faq.q: What does No.9 Hostel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start from about ฿350/night for a bed in a shared dorm. A 4-bed dorm bed is around ฿420, there's a female-only dorm at times, and you can book a whole dorm for a small group depending on bed count. Prices vary by season, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is No.9 Hostel a party hostel or a quiet one?
faq.a: It's a quiet, clean hostel rather than a party hostel. The common space is limited and the social-atmosphere score isn't high. It suits travellers who want a peaceful bed in a good location more than a social scene — if you want to meet fellow travellers every night, a more social hostel may suit you better.

faq.q: Who is No.9 Hostel best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for solo travellers, couples or budget backpackers who want a clean, quiet bed in a central location, walkable for sightseeing and easy to reach by train. If you want a private room with full amenities or a riverside setting, choose a guesthouse or higher-tier hotel instead.

faq.q: Is there a kitchen and washing machine I can use?
faq.a: Yes. No.9 Hostel has a shared kitchen, washing machine, communal fridge and microwave, plus a personal locker per bed. It's a feature longer-stay backpackers love, letting you cook and do laundry yourself to save money on the road.

faq.q: What should I know before booking No.9 Hostel?
faq.a: Key things: it's a small hostel with few beds that fill quickly on holidays, so book ahead. It's dorm-focused, so privacy is limited, and the atmosphere is quiet rather than lively. But the clear strengths are cleanliness, a caring owner, and a central location you can explore on foot.
